title: Quadratic phase forecasts for OGLE-LMC-LPV-40086 depend on the time split and baseline model
abstract: We test a steady frequency change as an explanation for poor fixed-period forecasts of the known red giant OGLE-LMC-LPV-40086. Early fits predict later public OGLE I photometry at three time splits. With two harmonics and all data, forecast gains over a fixed period are -11, 3 and -60 percent. An early offset changes the gains to 46, -25 and -431 percent. Thus an improved fit does not give a stable predictive drift in this scope. Later-only data, one-harmonic fits, two other known sources and sparse V measurements provide controls. Both bands use OGLE; independent instrument confirmation is absent. This is a restricted test of known long secondary period signals, not a new source or planet detection. Source measurements remain external. The bundle includes code, input hashes, aggregate results, a figure and retrieval steps.

display.caption: Later forecast gain and fitted local period derivative for OGLE-LMC-LPV-40086. The models use two harmonics. Results change with time split and baseline choice. The derivative is a local fit parameter, not a confirmed physical change.
